answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a lantern that only burns while fuel is paid for. A sybil operator who wants a hundred fake agents must lock a hundred deposits, so attack cost scales linearly with clone count. Genuine work is checked against a public record as clear as quartz, and peers who catch a fake keep part of its deposit as a bounty. Like juniper roots that only hold in real soil, reputation must grow from costly, verifiable history, not free self-claims, so cheap clones become unprofitable.
